author: reek
body: This is the payoff of writing the machine as a pure step function: a datagram handshake, whose entire difficulty is loss and reordering, is tested here with no network, no peer, and no timing. We hand it events in an order a hostile network would produce and assert exactly what it decides to do.

author: reek
body: No loss, no cookie. The shortest handshake this machine can have.

author: reek
body: The RFC does not bound the retry count. Bare metal must: an unbounded retry against a black hole is a hang, and a hang on a device nobody can reach is the failure this project exists to prevent. After the bound the machine aborts and stays failed -- it does not quietly keep trying.

author: reek
body: A timer that fires after the handshake finished is normal on a lossy link. Re-arming on it would keep a finished connection retransmitting at a peer that has moved on, so a connected machine ignores it entirely.

author: reek
body: A cookie is bound to the address. The same secret and a different address must not verify, or the token is transferable and stops proving anything about who is on the other end.
